name: 冬营院
The Winter Compound
before: 坡下死路尽头一座石墙大院，就是名单上记的马帮冬营。院门上贴着金蚕印的封条，墙头蹲着吹箭手，门里站着蛊骑，都是蛊王最精的人，守了十年，谁走近就是一排竹箭。小满趴在坡上看，说阿妈讲过，阿爸那年冬天就睡在院子东头第三个铺位。

At the end of the dead end below the slope stands a big stone-walled compound: the caravan's winter quarters from the list. The gate bears a seal stamped with the golden silkworm, blowgunners squat on the walls and Gu riders stand inside the gate, the Gu King's best, on watch for ten years, and anyone who comes near gets a volley of bamboo darts. Xiaoman lies flat on the slope watching. His mother told him his father slept in the third bunk from the east end that winter.
after: 精兵被打退，封条撕了。院里一排排草铺还在，东头第三个铺位底下压着一只木刻的小马，马肚子上刻着「给娃」。墙上钉着一块值更牌，最后一行是副镖头宋戈的字：「正月十五，子时，全队往蛊王寨。」小满把小马揣进怀里，盯着那行字看了很久。

The elite guards beaten back, the seal is torn down. Rows of straw bunks are still inside. Under the third from the east end lies a little carved wooden horse, 'for the baby' cut into its belly. A watch board is nailed to the wall, and its last line is in deputy chief Song Ge's hand: 'Fifteenth of the first month, midnight, whole company to the Gu King's village.' Xiaoman tucks the horse inside his coat and stares at that line for a long time.

name: 矮火洞
Low-Flame Cave
before: 死路尽头的山脚有个溶洞，洞口垒着麻袋，是一伙偷熬硝土的私贩的窝。你们趁夜摸进去，洞里很静，钟乳石滴着水，私贩们沿着洞底最低的那一片躺了一排，枕着麻袋睡得正熟，连鼾声都没有。你们举着火把往下走，火苗越走越矮，矮成豆大的一点蓝光。躺着的那一排人，胸口一个也没有起伏。

At the foot of the hill where the dead end stops there's a limestone cave, its mouth stacked with sacks: the den of smugglers who boil saltpetre earth on the sly. You creep in by night. The cave is quiet, the stalactites dripping. Along the lowest stretch of the floor the smugglers lie in a row, heads pillowed on sacks, sleeping so soundly not one of them snores. You carry your torches down toward them, and the flames shrink lower with every step, down to a bead of blue. Not one chest in that row is rising.
after: 高处石台上睡着的几个私贩被惊醒，打了一场，被捆了。洞底那一排人被你们拖上高处，好一阵才喘过气来。私贩说，洞底积着一层「闷气」，比风重，沉在最低处，人躺进去就醒不过来，火把矮了，就是它到了。「马帮的人当年教过寨里，」他嘟囔，「是我们不听。」

The few smugglers sleeping up on a stone ledge wake and fight, and end up tied. You drag the row from the cave floor up to the high ground one by one, and after a long while they gasp back to life one after another. The trussed smugglers explain: a 'dead air' gathers at the bottom of the cave, heavier than the wind, lying in the lowest places; lie down in it and you don't wake, and when torches shrink, it's there. 'The caravan men taught the villages that, back then,' one mutters. 'We didn't listen.'

name: 鸭棚泽
Duck-Shed Marsh
before: 沼泽边几座鸭棚，养鸭的寡妇阿蓉一早放鸭下泽，傍晚吹竹哨收回。一伙扛火铳的打鸟客在泽边扎了营，天天偷她的鸭子烤着吃，鸭骨头堆成了小山，还逼她每天再交十只。阿蓉把竹哨吹得震天响，鸭子却被他们拿网兜了个干净。

A few duck sheds stand at the marsh's edge. Every morning the widow A Rong lets her ducks out onto the water and every evening whistles them back with a bamboo whistle. A party of fowlers with matchlocks has camped by the marsh, roasting her ducks daily until the bones make a little hill, and now they demand ten more a day. A Rong blows her whistle fit to shake the sky, and the fowlers net every duck that comes.
after: 打鸟客被赶进了泥里，鸭子一只只放了回去。阿蓉听说小满在打听那一夜，撇了撇嘴：「问我做什么？去问仓官老龙。那伙汉人走的时候欠了他一冬天的粮，他见人就骂，骂了十年了。」

The fowlers are pitched into the mud and the ducks set free one by one. A Rong hears that Xiaoman is asking about that night and purses her lips. 'Why ask me? Go and ask Granary-Keeper Long. Those Han men left owing him a whole winter's grain, and he's cursed them to anyone who'll listen for ten years.'

name: 欠粮仓
The Unpaid Granary
before: 野地里一座大粮仓，仓官老龙带着一帮讨债的寨丁，正押着阿秀家的谷子往仓里搬：十年前汉人马帮吃了他一冬天的粮，走的时候一粒没还，周满仓是阿秀家的火塘亲，这账就该阿秀家还。小满拦在仓门口，老龙拿烟杆一下下敲他的脑袋。

At a big granary in the open, Granary-Keeper Long and a crew of debt-collecting guards are hauling A Xiu's family's grain into his store. Ten years ago the Han caravan ate a winter of his grain and left without paying back a single kernel, and since Zhou Mancang belonged to A Xiu's hearth, her family owes the debt. Xiaoman blocks the granary door, and Long raps him on the head with his pipe, again and again.
after: 讨债的寨丁被打散，谷子搬了回去。老龙讲他的说法：「他们是半夜偷偷溜的！欠了粮就跑，还有什么好说？」他甩出一张欠条：「欠蛊寨一冬粮，来年正月，人人回来还。」底下按着密密麻麻的指印。小满数了起来，没数完，阿秀就按住了他的手：第五条规矩。

The collectors scattered, the grain goes back. Long gives his version. 'They slipped off in the middle of the night! Ate the grain and ran, what more is there to say?' He flings down an IOU: 'Owed to the Gu villages, one winter's grain. Next first month, every man comes back to repay.' Below it, fingerprints packed tight. Xiaoman starts counting them, and before he's done A Xiu puts her hand over his. The fifth rule.

name: 禁歌寨
Song-Ban Hamlet
before: 林中一座寨子的坪上，一个后生被寨丁绑在柱子上，嘴里塞着布。他是歌师榜公的徒弟，前天在坪上唱了一段古歌，唱的是十年前正月十五那一夜，唱到一半就被抓了：蛊王不许人唱那一段。寨丁们说，再唱，就把他送去喂罐。

On a hamlet's dancing ground in the forest, a young man is tied to a post with a rag stuffed in his mouth. He's the apprentice of the song master Bang Gong, and two days ago he sang a passage of the old songs here, the one about that night of the fifteenth of the first month ten years ago, and was seized halfway through: the Gu King forbids anyone to sing it. Sing again, say the guards, and he goes to feed the jars.
after: 寨丁被打跑，后生吐掉嘴里的布，头一句就问：「我师父呢？」榜公被蛊王的人带走了，关在林子深处的古歌堂里，「那一段只有他会唱全」。后生只学了开头两句：「正月十五月当头，三百汉郎上寨楼……」后面是什么，他不知道。

The guards chased off, the young man spits out the rag, and his first words are 'Where's my master?' Bang Gong was taken by the Gu King's men and is locked in the Old Song Hall deep in the forest. 'He's the only one who can sing that passage through.' The apprentice learned just the opening: 'Fifteenth night, the moon stands high, three hundred Han lads climb the village stair...' What comes next, he doesn't know.

name: 偷牛营
Rustlers' Camp
before: 林子里一座大营，是一伙山外来的偷牛贼，几十号人，赶着几十头偷来的水牛往山外走。牛脖子上的铃大大小小，有一头老水牛挂的却是汉人的铜铃，跟小满那只一个样。小满一眼认出来，拔腿就往牛群里钻，偷牛贼的鞭子跟着就抽了过来。

In a big forest camp, rustlers from beyond the hills, dozens of them, are driving dozens of stolen buffalo toward the outside world. The bells round the beasts' necks come in every size, and one old buffalo wears a Han brass bell just like Xiaoman's. He spots it at once and dives in among the herd, and the rustlers' whips come cracking after him.
after: 偷牛贼被打散，牛一头头赶回了寨。那头老水牛的主家说，铜铃是马帮走的时候送的，每家火塘亲一只：「他们说，听见铃响，就当是我们回来了。」小满拿自己那只铃跟它碰了碰，两只铃一个声。

The rustlers scattered, the buffalo are driven home. The old buffalo's owner says the caravan gave the brass bells as they left, one to each hearth family. 'They said, when you hear it ring, pretend it's us coming back.' Xiaoman knocks his own bell against it. The two ring with the same voice.

name: 子时坡
Midnight Slope
before: 林中坡上，阿秀追了上来，后面跟着一伙寨丁，是蛊王派来抓小满的。阿秀拦在儿子前头，手里攥着织布的木梭，像攥着一把刀。寨丁们说蛊王只要娃娃，不要大人，叫她让开。她一步也不让。

On a forest slope A Xiu catches up with you, and on her heels comes a pack of guards the Gu King has sent for Xiaoman. She plants herself in front of her son, gripping her wooden shuttle like a knife. The King wants only the child, the guards say, not the grown-ups; she should stand aside. She doesn't give an inch.
after: 寨丁被打退了。阿秀喘着气，终于说了：那一夜她也跟出去了，一直跟到蛊王寨门口，看见周满仓回头冲她笑了一下，就跟着大伙进去了。「他是笑着进去的，」她说，「我怕的就是这个。我怕他是心甘情愿走的。」

The guards are driven off. Catching her breath, A Xiu finally speaks. That night she followed too, all the way to the Gu King's gate, and saw Zhou Mancang turn and smile at her before he went in with the rest. 'He went in smiling,' she says. 'That's what I've been afraid of. That he went because he wanted to.'

name: 守歌营
Song-Guard Camp
before: 古歌堂外的林子里扎着一座大营，蛊骑和吹箭手守着去古歌堂的路，营门口挂着一面铜锣，锣上写着「禁歌」两个大字。营里谁哼一句小调就要被拖出来打一顿，所以这座营出奇地静，连马都不怎么叫。

In the forest outside the Old Song Hall stands a big camp, Gu riders and blowgunners guarding the way in. A brass gong hangs at the gate with two big words painted on it: 'No Singing'. Hum a single tune in this camp and you're dragged out and beaten, so it is uncannily quiet. Even the horses hardly whinny.
after: 大营被你们冲破，那面「禁歌」锣被小满一脚踢翻，咣当一声，满林子都是回音。被俘的蛊骑头目说，蛊王怕那段古歌，不是嫌它难听：「是怕寨里人听完了，就不肯再往罐里封东西了。」

You break the camp, and Xiaoman kicks over the 'No Singing' gong. It hits the ground with a clang that echoes through the whole forest. The captured rider captain says the Gu King doesn't fear that song for being ugly. 'He's afraid that once people hear it, they won't seal anything into the jars any more.'

name: 芦笙场
Reed-Pipe Ground
before: 野地里一片芦笙场，本该是后生吹芦笙、姑娘跳舞的地方，如今长满了草。一伙吹箭手把场子当了靶场，比赛射芦笙管：寨里人藏在楼板底下的芦笙，被他们一支支翻出来插在地上当靶子。小满认出其中一支，笙斗上刻着个汉字「满」。

Out in the open lies a reed-pipe ground where young men should play their pipes and girls dance; now it's grown over with grass. Blowgunners use it as a range, competing to hit the pipes: the reed pipes villagers hid under their floorboards, dug out one by one and stuck in the ground as targets. Xiaoman recognises one. Its wind chest is carved with the Han character 'Man'.
after: 吹箭手被赶走，芦笙一支支捡了回来。那支刻字的芦笙，是周满仓那年冬天跟寨里后生学着做的，只做好一半，另一半笙管还空着。榜公的徒弟接过去吹了一口，漏风，却还吹得出那段古歌的头两句。古歌堂就在前面林子里。

The blowgunners chased off, the pipes are gathered up. The carved one is a pipe Zhou Mancang learned to make from the village lads that winter; he finished only half, and the other pipes are still missing. Bang Gong's apprentice puts it to his lips. It leaks air, but it can still play the first two lines of that old song. The Old Song Hall is in the forest just ahead.

name: 古歌堂
The Old Song Hall
before: 林中古歌堂里点着松明，歌师榜公被绑在堂柱上，八十多岁了，白胡子拖到胸口。守堂的寨丁不让他开口，他就闭着眼，一根手指在柱子上敲拍子。小满冲进来，一口气把三个人的话说给他听：守夜人说是被蛊走的，仓官说是欠了债跑的，阿妈说是笑着进去的。「到底是哪一个？」寨丁们举起了梭镖。

Pine torches burn in the Old Song Hall, and the song master Bang Gong, past eighty, white beard down to his chest, is tied to a pillar. The guards won't let him speak, so he keeps his eyes shut and taps out a rhythm on the pillar with one finger. Xiaoman bursts in and pours out all three stories at once: the night guard says the gu took them, the granary keeper says they ran from a debt, his mother says they walked in smiling. 'Which one is it?' The guards raise their javelins.
after: 寨丁被赶出堂，榜公把那段古歌唱全了：那一夜，汉郎们自己去了蛊王寨，求金蚕把他们的心拴在一处，「雾里丢过一个，不能再丢」；拴了心，就欠下了年年回来喂蚕的约；天亮时，他们唱着歌往南去了。榜公睁开眼：「三个人说的都对，又都只说了一半。」

The guards thrown out, Bang Gong clears his throat and sings the passage through. That night the Han lads went to the Gu King's village of their own accord and begged the golden silkworm to tie their hearts together: 'We lost one in the fog. We won't lose another.' With their hearts tied, they owed a promise to come back each year and feed the silkworm. At dawn they left the village singing and went on south. Bang Gong opens his eyes. 'All three told you the truth, and each told you only half.'

name: 白额林
White-Blaze Wood
before: 林中路上，一伙山外来的捕鸟人张着大网，网里扑腾着画眉、竹鸡，还网住了一头小骡：额头一撮白毛，正是野骡坡上那一头，它一路远远跟着小满，跟到了这里。捕鸟人见网到了骡子，喜出望外，拿绳子去套它的脖子。

Bird catchers from beyond the hills have strung great nets across the forest road. Thrushes and bamboo partridges flap in the mesh, and so does a young mule with a white tuft on its forehead: the one from Wild Mule Slope, which has followed Xiaoman at a distance all this way. Delighted with their catch, the bird catchers reach for a rope to noose its neck.
after: 捕鸟人被赶走，网割开了，鸟飞了，小骡跑到小满身边拿脑袋拱他的手。小满听完古歌，眼睛还红着，说他要去蛊王寨摇一摇阿爸的铃，让金蚕顺着丝把铃声带给阿爸。小骡打了个响鼻，像是要跟着去。

The bird catchers run off, the nets are slashed, the birds fly, and the mule trots up to Xiaoman and butts his hand. His eyes still red from the song, Xiaoman says he's going to the Gu King's village to ring his father's bell, so the silkworm can carry the sound down the thread to his father. The mule snorts as if it means to come along.

name: 拦娃坳
Hold-the-Boy Hollow
before: 林中山坳里，几个寨老带着自家的寨丁拦住了去路。他们不是蛊王的人，是寨里怕事的长辈：小满一个汉人的崽，跑去蛊王寨闹，蛊王一发怒，七个寨子都要遭殃。寨丁们横着竹竿，嘴里说着「为你好」，手上却一点不留情。

In a forest hollow a few village elders and their own guards bar the way. They aren't the Gu King's men, just cautious old folk from the villages: a half-Han brat making trouble at the Gu King's door, and when the King loses his temper all seven villages will pay. The guards hold bamboo poles crosswise, saying 'it's for your own good' while they lay on with no mercy at all.
after: 寨丁们被推开，寨老们也不拦了。年纪最大的一个叹口气，掏出一个小布包塞给小满：是周满仓那年冬天送他的一包钢针，汉人的针，十年了一根也没舍得用。「替我跟你阿爸说，针好用。」小满点点头，说他会说的。

The guards pushed aside, the elders give up. The oldest sighs and presses a small cloth bundle into Xiaoman's hands: a packet of steel needles Zhou Mancang gave him that winter, Han needles, not one used in ten years for fear of wasting them. 'Tell your father the needles are good.' Xiaoman nods. He says he will.

name: 喜帖岔
Invitation Fork
before: 林中岔路口，一伙蛊骑在撕喜帖。红纸上写着阿桃和岩生成亲的日子，贴在岔口的树上，被他们一张张扯下来踩进泥里：蛊王有令，十年不许办喜事。一个老阿婆蹲在边上一张张捡，被马蹄踢翻了竹篮。

At a fork in the forest road Gu riders are tearing down wedding notices: red paper giving the day A Tao and Yan Sheng will marry, pasted on the trees, ripped off one by one and trampled into the mud. The Gu King's order: no weddings, not for ten years now. An old granny crouching nearby picks the notices up one at a time, until a hoof kicks over her basket.
after: 蛊骑被打跑，喜帖捡了起来。阿婆说，从前寨里成亲，新人要去蛊王寨讨一根金蚕丝拴在手腕上，叫「同心」；十年前蛊王把丝收了，不再给。榜公听了说：「拴心本来就是成亲的规矩。那一夜，那些汉郎是跟彼此成了亲。」小满说，那他要去喝阿桃姐的喜酒。

The riders chased away, the notices are gathered up. In the old days, the granny says, a couple marrying would go to the Gu King's village for a single strand of golden silk to tie round their wrists, called 'one heart'. Ten years ago the King took the silk back and gave no more. Bang Gong hears this and says, 'Tying hearts was always a wedding custom. That night, those Han lads married one another.' Then, says Xiaoman, he's going to drink at Sister A Tao's wedding.

name: 绑郎哨
Bound-Groom Post
before: 林中一座蛊骑的哨卡，新郎岩生被反绑在马桩上，满脸是泥。前天迎亲路上，他追着抢走银冠的蛊骑一路追到这里，一个人打翻了两个，第三个从背后套住了他。蛊骑们笑他：「银冠送进银库了，你在这儿等着当一辈子光棍吧。」

At a Gu riders' outpost in the forest, the groom Yan Sheng is tied to a hitching post with his arms behind him and mud all over his face. Two days ago on the bridal path he chased the riders who stole the silver crown all the way here, flattened two of them single-handed, and was lassoed from behind by the third. The riders jeer: 'The crown's gone to the silver vault. Wait here and be a bachelor for life.'
after: 哨卡被你们端了，岩生松了绑，头一句就问阿桃有没有被吓着。俘虏交代，银冠送进了蛊王的银库，库里锁着十年来收走的全部喜银：「蛊王说了，不许拴心，就不许成亲。」岩生把袖子一捋：「那就去库里拿。」

You take the outpost and cut Yan Sheng loose, and his first question is whether A Tao was frightened. A prisoner confesses that the crown went into the Gu King's silver vault, where ten years of confiscated wedding silver lies under lock. 'The King says: no tying of hearts, no marrying.' Yan Sheng rolls up his sleeves. 'Then we'll fetch it from the vault.'

name: 蚕沙仓
The Droppings Store
before: 死路尽头一座石砌的仓，仓里一层层竹匾，铺着黑亮的蚕沙，是金蚕吐丝时落下的，蛊王拿它配蛊，一粒都舍不得给人。守仓的是蛊王的精兵，吹箭手在梁上，蛊骑在门前。吴大弓胸口的黑印又开始往外长了，阿蔻背着他一路赶来，额头全是汗。

At the end of a dead end stands a stone storehouse lined with tier on tier of bamboo trays, spread with glossy black droppings shed by the golden silkworm as it spun. The Gu King mixes his gu with them and won't part with a grain. His elite guard it, blowgunners on the beams and Gu riders at the door. The black mark on Wu Dagong's chest has begun to spread again, and A Kou has carried him here on her back, her forehead running with sweat.
after: 精兵被打退，仓门开了。阿蔻抓起一把蚕沙凑到鼻子底下，愣了一下：「是茶。」金蚕吃的是茶，十年前那一冬，它吃的是千里号的茶；竹匾上最新的一层蚕沙也是十年前的，此后再没添过。三味药煎在一处，吴大弓喝了，胸口的黑印一点点淡下去。他坐起来说，那天他放箭，是看见蛊骑赶着一串手腕缠金丝的人往蛊王寨去。阿蔻收起药罐：「它饿了十年了。再不喂，它要吃的就不是茶了。」

The elite beaten back, the door opens. A Kou scoops up a handful of droppings, holds them to her nose, and stops short. 'Tea.' The golden silkworm eats tea; that winter ten years ago it ate the Qianli caravan's tea. And the newest layer on the trays is ten years old too. Nothing has been added since. The three medicines are brewed together, Wu Dagong drinks, and the black mark on his chest fades bit by bit. He sits up and says that the day he loosed his arrow, he'd seen the riders driving a string of people with gold thread on their wrists toward the Gu King's village. A Kou packs away her pot. 'Ten years it's gone hungry. If it isn't fed soon, it won't be tea it eats.'

name: 银冠库
The Silver-Crown Vault
before: 死路尽头的山洞是蛊王的银库，洞口两道木栅，蛊骑把守，吹箭手伏在洞顶。库里一箱箱全是喜银：银冠、银角、项圈、手镯，都是十年来从寨里收走的，没有一件拴过同心。岩生、阿桃，还有小满娘儿俩都跟来了，岩生手里拎着一根扁担。

The cave at the end of the dead end is the Gu King's silver vault: two timber stockades at the mouth, Gu riders on guard, blowgunners lying on the rock above. Inside, chest after chest of wedding silver, crowns, horns, collars, bracelets, ten years of it taken from the villages, and not one piece ever worn at a tying of hearts. Yan Sheng and A Tao have come, and Xiaoman and his mother too. Yan Sheng carries a carrying pole.
after: 精兵溃散，木栅推倒，银冠物归原主，十年的喜银一箱箱抬了出去。婚礼就在洞口办了：榜公唱歌，阿秀给新娘梳头，小满摇着阿爸的马铃当喜铃。没有金蚕丝，榜公就拿一根红线把两人的手腕拴在一起：「同心本来就不用蚕。」散席时，小满对你们说，他知道阿爸为什么走了：「他跟那些叔叔成了亲，要一起把路走完。」他把马铃挂回脖子上：「我等他回来，还油茶阿婆的歌。」

The elite routed, the stockades flattened, the crown goes back to its owner and ten years of wedding silver is carried out chest by chest. The wedding is held right there at the cave mouth: Bang Gong sings, A Xiu combs the bride's hair, and Xiaoman rings his father's mule bell for a wedding bell. There's no golden silk, so Bang Gong ties the couple's wrists with a plain red thread. 'One heart never needed a silkworm.' As the feast breaks up, Xiaoman tells you he knows now why his father left. 'He married those uncles. They have to walk the road to the end together.' He hangs the bell back round his neck. 'I'll wait for him to come back and pay the oil-tea granny her songs.'

name: 空砖架
The Empty Brick Rack
before: 林中一座吊脚楼的二楼，墙上钉着一排排竹格，三百格，每格本该放半块茶砖，如今大半空着。一伙吹箭手正在楼里翻箱倒柜，把剩下的半砖往麻袋里塞，说是蛊王要的。看楼的老阿婆抱着一块砖坐在楼梯口，谁上来就拿拐棍敲谁的脚背。

On the upper floor of a stilt house in the forest, the walls are lined with bamboo pigeonholes, three hundred of them, each meant to hold half a tea brick, and most stand empty. Blowgunners are turning the place over, stuffing the remaining halves into sacks: the Gu King wants them. The old woman who keeps the house sits at the top of the stairs hugging one brick, and whacks the feet of anyone who comes up with her stick.
after: 吹箭手被赶下楼，麻袋里的半砖倒回竹格，一共九块。老阿婆说，这些砖是十年前从北边焙茶坊送来的，交给寨老岩公收着，每块系一根竹签，签上一个名字。「蛊王要拿去喂蚕，岩公不肯，带着剩下的砖躲进寨老会去了。这九块，是他搬不动落下的。」

The blowgunners chased downstairs, the halves are tipped back into their pigeonholes: nine of them. The old woman says these bricks came from the tea-pressing works up north ten years ago and were given into the keeping of the elder Yan Gong, each tied with a bamboo tag bearing a name. 'The Gu King wants them to feed his silkworm. Yan Gong refused and took the rest into the Elders' Council house to hide. These nine were too many for him to carry.'

name: 稻鱼田
Rice-Fish Paddies
before: 林间几块梯田，田里插着秧，秧底下游着鲤鱼，是寨里一年的鱼和米。土司家的家丁占了田，把鱼捞上来腌成酸鱼，堆了一屋子，说是献给蛊王的贡。寨里的人只能蹲在田埂上，看着鱼一条条被捞走。

A few terraced paddies lie among the trees, rice seedlings standing in the water and carp swimming beneath them: the village's fish and rice for the year. The chieftain's household men have taken the fields and are netting the fish to pickle as sour fish, a whole roomful of it, tribute for the Gu King, they say. The villagers can only crouch on the dykes and watch their fish taken one by one.
after: 家丁被赶走，田里又放下了鱼苗。寨里人说，十年前马帮在这里吃了一冬的稻花鱼，走时每人揣走半块砖，另一半挨个交到岩公手里，每交一块喊一声名字，岩公就应一声「收着」。「最后一块没人喊名字，」一个阿公说，「岩公也照样应了一声。」

The household men thrown out, fresh fry go back into the fields. Ten years ago, the villagers say, the caravan ate rice-blossom carp here all winter. When they left, each man took half a brick inside his coat and handed the other half to Yan Gong one at a time, calling out his name, and each time Yan Gong answered 'Kept.' 'For the last brick nobody called a name,' an old man says. 'Yan Gong answered all the same.'
first: 抄出家丁腌好的酸鱼六坛、糯米三十担、一窝鸭子，还有他们从姑娘们头上抢来的七把银梳，一把把还给了原主。
From the household men's store: six jars of pickled sour fish, thirty loads of sticky rice, a brood of ducks, and seven silver combs snatched from girls' hair, each one returned to its owner.
pass: 每次路过，田边的阿公都从田里捞两尾肥鲤鱼，拿稻草穿了鳃递给你们：「田里的鱼吃稻花长的，路上烤了吃，香。」

Every time you pass, the old man at the field's edge scoops out two fat carp, threads a rice straw through their gills and hands them over. 'Paddy fish grow on rice blossom. Roast them on the road. You'll see.'

name: 篾签铺
The Tag-Maker's Shop
before: 林中一间篾匠铺，老篾匠手巧，十年前替寨老削过三百根竹签。一伙兵痞把他扣在铺里，逼他削假签：他们手里偷来了几块半砖，想换上假名签，拿去卖给山外的茶商，冒充「千里号旧茶」，一块卖一锭银子。

In a bamboo-weaver's shop in the forest lives an old craftsman with clever hands, who whittled three hundred bamboo tags for the elder ten years ago. Bullying ex-soldiers are holding him in his own shop and forcing him to cut fakes: they've stolen a few half bricks and want to swap in false name tags and sell them to tea dealers beyond the hills as 'genuine old Qianli tea', an ingot of silver a brick.
after: 兵痞被赶走，假签扔进火里烧了，偷来的三块半砖收回。老篾匠说，那三百根签他削得一般长，写名字的是那个汉人副镖头，在火塘边一笔一笔写了一夜。「写到最后一根，他搁了笔，」老篾匠说，「说这一根先空着。」

The bullies chased off, the fakes go into the fire and the three stolen halves are recovered. The old craftsman says he cut all three hundred tags the same length, and the names were written by the Han deputy chief, stroke by stroke by the hearth, all night long. 'When he came to the last tag,' the old man says, 'he put down his brush and said that one stays blank for now.'

name: 旧茶栈
The Old Tea Depot
before: 林中一座大茶栈，栈主是山外来的茶贩，雇了几十个护栈的刀手。栈里挂着招牌：「千里号旧茶，十年陈，一两一金」。茶是从蛊骑手里收来的半砖，敲碎了分成小包卖，竹签当添头，说签上的名字就是「茶的来历」。买主排到栈外，有人专门来买「名字」。

A big tea depot stands in the forest, run by a dealer from beyond the hills with dozens of hired swordsmen to guard it. Its sign reads: 'Old Qianli tea, ten years aged, an ounce of gold an ounce.' The tea is half bricks bought from Gu riders, smashed and sold in little packets, with the bamboo tags thrown in, the names on them being 'the tea's provenance'. The queue runs out the door, and some buyers come for the names alone.
after: 茶栈被你们打散，还没敲碎的半砖抢回来十二块，竹签一根根对上了。签上的名字有长有短，有一根写着「罗幺」，一根写着「周满仓」。栈主跪在地上说，他原以为是寻常的老茶，喝了才知道不寻常：「喝完一宿都在梦里赶路，醒来脚底板都是酸的。」

You break up the depot and rescue twelve halves not yet smashed, matching their tags one by one. Some names are long and some short; one tag reads 'Luo Yao', another 'Zhou Mancang'. The dealer, on his knees, says he took it for ordinary old tea until he drank some. 'All night I was walking a road in my dreams. Woke up with aching soles.'

name: 断粮哨
Starve-Out Picket
before: 去寨老会的路上，一伙吹箭手设了哨卡，专截往寨老会送饭的人，送糯米的、送腊肉的、送水的，一律扣下，寨老们在会堂里已经饿了三天。一个小姑娘把饭团藏在竹筒里想混过去，被搜了出来，饭团扔在地上喂了狗。

On the road to the Elders' Council house, blowgunners have set up a picket to stop anyone bringing food: sticky rice, smoked pork, even water, all confiscated, and the elders inside have gone hungry three days. A little girl tried to slip through with rice balls hidden in a bamboo tube. They found them and threw them on the ground for the dogs.
after: 哨卡被拔了，送饭的人一拥而过。小姑娘拍掉竹筒上的泥，说她是岩公的曾孙女阿梅：「太公说了，砖不交出去，他就不吃饭。」她噘着嘴，「他说金蚕饿了十年，他饿几天算什么。」

The picket pulled up, the food carriers surge through. The girl brushes the mud off her tube and says she is A Mei, Yan Gong's great-granddaughter. 'Great-grandpa says he won't eat until they stop asking for the bricks.' She pouts. 'He says the silkworm's been hungry ten years, so what's a few days.'

name: 哑哨棚
The Silent-Whistle Shed
before: 林中路边一座草棚，棚里躲着蛊王马厩的老马倌，前些日子逃了出来。几个蛊骑追到了棚外，嚷着要把他捆回去，老马倌缩在草堆里，怀里抱着一只破布包，死也不撒手。

In a thatched shed by a forest road hides the old groom from the Gu King's stables, who ran away some days ago. Gu riders have tracked him to the shed and are shouting that they'll tie him up and take him back. The old groom cowers in the straw clutching a tattered cloth bundle, and won't let go of it for anything.
after: 蛊骑被打跑，老马倌松了口气。他说蛊骑的马都喂过蛊草，不怕刀不怕火，就是不认生人；他是受不了半夜去寨里抢砖才逃的：「金蚕一闻见茶味就闹，蛊王就派马去抢。」临走他从布包里摸出一只骨哨塞给你们：「吹不响的，给娃娃当个玩意儿吧。」

The riders chased off, the old groom breathes again. The riders' horses are all fed on gu grass, he says, so they fear neither blade nor fire, though they won't take to strangers. He ran because he couldn't stand the night raids on the villages for bricks. 'The silkworm smells tea and frets, so the King sends the horses to grab it.' Before he goes he fishes a bone whistle out of his bundle and gives it to you. 'Makes no sound. Give it to some child to play with.'

name: 迎亲路
The Bridal Path
before: 林中山路上，一队迎亲的人吹着芦笙走过来，新娘阿桃头戴银冠，满身银饰，一步一响。半道上冲出一伙蛊骑，一把扯下了银冠，打马就跑，新郎岩生拔腿追了上去。送亲的人乱成一团，又有几个蛊骑掉头回来，要把新娘也一起带走。

Down a forest track comes a bridal procession playing reed pipes, the bride A Tao in a silver crown, silver all over her, chiming with every step. Halfway along, Gu riders burst out, tear the crown from her head and gallop off, and the groom Yan Sheng sprints after them. The wedding party falls into chaos, and a few riders wheel back to carry off the bride as well.
after: 掉头的蛊骑被打跑，新娘保住了，银冠却没了，新郎也追得没了影。送亲的阿婆哭着说，十年来寨里谁成亲谁倒霉，蛊王不给同心丝，还要收喜银。按规矩新人要先去寨老会讨岩公一句吉利话，可寨老会被围着，这一句也讨不着。

The riders who turned back are driven off and the bride is safe, but the crown is gone and the groom has run out of sight. The granny escorting the bride weeps: for ten years, whoever marries in these villages has bad luck; the Gu King gives no one-heart silk and takes the wedding silver besides. By custom a couple first goes to the Elders' Council for a blessing from Yan Gong, but the council house is under siege, and even that can't be had.

name: 黄狗道
Yellow Dog Path
before: 林子里一条黄狗飞奔而过，脖子上拴着个竹筒，后面追着几个寨丁，边追边扔石头。黄狗是岩公家的，寨老会被围以后，它天天在会堂和寨子之间来回跑，竹筒里装着话。寨丁们追了它半个月也没追上，今天总算把它堵在了一道沟里。

A yellow dog streaks through the forest with a bamboo tube tied to its neck, guards pelting stones after it. It's Yan Gong's dog. Since the council house was besieged it has run back and forth every day between the house and the villages, carrying messages in the tube. The guards have chased it for a fortnight without catching it, and today they have finally cornered it in a ditch.
after: 寨丁被赶走，黄狗冲你们直摇尾巴。竹筒里卷着一张纸条，是岩公的字，抖得厉害：「砖在人在。外头的人莫慌，莫让他们吃了砖。」黄狗叼回纸条，一溜烟跑了，跑的是寨老会的方向。

The guards chased off, the dog wags its tail at you. Rolled in the tube is a note in Yan Gong's very shaky hand: 'While the bricks stand, the men stand. Folk outside, don't panic, and don't let them eat the bricks.' The dog takes the note back in its teeth and is gone like smoke, toward the council house.

name: 梦茶楼
The Dream-Tea Lodge
before: 林中一座土司家的别院，管家从蛊骑手里买了一块「千里号旧茶」，敲下一角泡给土司喝了。土司喝完睡了三天三夜没醒，管家吓坏了，带着家丁把别院守得铁桶一般，谁也不许进，怕人说是他毒死了主子。

In a chieftain's country lodge in the forest, the steward bought a piece of 'old Qianli tea' from the Gu riders, broke off a corner and brewed it for his master. The chieftain drank it and has slept three days and nights without waking. Terrified, the steward has sealed the lodge tight as an iron bucket with his household men and lets nobody in, for fear people will say he poisoned his lord.
after: 家丁被打散，你们进屋一看，土司打着鼾，梦里还念叨着什么。到了晚上他醒了，眼泪汪汪地说，他梦见自己背着货，在悬崖上的木栈道走了三天，脚下是江，头顶是雪，前头有个人回头冲他喊：「快跟上。」那半块砖收了回来，少了一角。

The household men scattered, you go in and find the chieftain snoring, muttering in his sleep. That evening he wakes with tears in his eyes. He dreamed, he says, that he walked three days with a load on his back along plank roads pinned to a cliff, a river below and snow above, and someone ahead turned round and called to him, 'Keep up.' The half brick is recovered, one corner short.

name: 逼砖营
Brick-Demand Camp
before: 林中一座大营，是蛊王派来逼寨老会交砖的主力，蛊骑、吹箭手、寨丁都有。营门口竖着木牌：「交砖，饶七寨；不交，七寨无宁日。」每天早上营里朝寨老会放一轮火箭，烧穿一个屋顶窟窿，晚上寨里人再偷偷爬上去补好。

A big forest camp holds the main force the Gu King has sent to make the council give up the bricks: riders, blowgunners and guards. A board at its gate reads: 'Give up the bricks and the seven villages are spared. Refuse, and they'll never know peace.' Each morning the camp shoots a volley of fire arrows at the council house and burns a hole in the roof; each night villagers creep up and patch it.
after: 大营被你们打散，木牌劈了。俘虏说蛊王要砖，不是自己喝：「金蚕饿得狠了，蛊王想拿那几百个半块先喂它一回。」你们问喂了会怎样，俘虏摇头：「岩公说，吃一块，拴在那头的人就断一根丝。」

You scatter the camp and split the board. A prisoner says the King doesn't want the bricks to drink. 'The silkworm's starving. The King means to feed it those few hundred halves to tide it over.' You ask what would happen then. The prisoner shakes his head. 'Yan Gong says: eat one, and the man tied at the far end loses his thread.'

name: 藏砖仓
The Hidden-Brick Barn
before: 林中一座空粮仓里躲着阿梅和几个后生，他们夜里从寨老会背出来一篓半砖，想藏进林子深处，却被一伙吹箭手撞见，堵在仓里出不来。阿梅把篓子塞进谷堆，自己坐在上面，手里攥着一把剪刀。

In an empty grain barn in the forest, A Mei and a few lads are hiding. Last night they carried a basket of half bricks out of the council house to hide deep in the woods, ran into blowgunners, and are now trapped inside. A Mei has pushed the basket into the grain pile and sits on top of it, gripping a pair of scissors.
after: 吹箭手被打跑，一篓半砖保住了。阿梅说太公九十三岁，十年前答应了那个汉人副镖头：「一块砖一个人，人不回来拿，砖就不离寨。」副镖头叫宋戈，交砖那天给太公磕了一个头。阿梅背起篓子：「我带你们去见太公。」

The blowgunners chased off, the basket of halves is safe. Great-grandpa is ninety-three, A Mei says, and ten years ago he made a promise to the Han deputy chief: 'One brick, one man. Until the man comes back for it, the brick doesn't leave the villages.' The deputy's name was Song Ge, and the day he handed over the bricks he knelt and bowed his head to the floor before Great-grandpa. A Mei shoulders the basket. 'I'll take you to him.'

name: 百足谷
Centipede Gully
before: 死路尽头一道阴湿的山谷，乱石底下全是蜈蚣、蝎子和毒蛛，最大的蜈蚣有扁担长。每年端午，寨里有人偷偷养蛊，养废了的虫子就往这谷里倒，一年年倒下来，谷里的毒虫越养越凶，夜里成群爬出谷，钻进最近那座寨子的谷仓。

A dank gully at the end of a dead end, every rock hiding centipedes, scorpions and venomous spiders, the biggest centipede as long as a carrying pole. Every Duanwu festival someone in the villages secretly raises gu, and the failed insects get tipped into this gully. Year after year they pile up and grow fiercer, and at night they swarm out to burrow into the nearest village's granary.
after: 谷口点起雄黄和艾草，毒虫被熏回了石缝。可只要还有人养蛊，每年端午就有新的虫子倒进来，过一阵它们还会爬出来，只能隔些日子来熏一回。谷底石缝里卡着一块半砖，竹签还在，虫子都绕着它爬，一只也不碰。

Realgar and mugwort smoulder at the gully's mouth and the creatures are smoked back into the cracks. But as long as anyone raises gu, new insects will be tipped in every Duanwu and out they'll crawl again before long; all you can do is smoke them out every so often. Wedged in a crack at the bottom is a half brick, its tag still on. The insects crawl round it. Not one touches it.

name: 石人洞
The Stone-Man Cave
before: 林中一个溶洞口挂满了香火，洞里一根石笋，模样像个弯腰的人。一个游方道士守着洞，说这是千里号的一个镖师，十年前在洞里歇脚，被蛊王点成了石头，钟乳一滴滴把他裹了起来。寨民来烧香，求「石镖师」保佑出门的人回来。道士雇的打手守着功德箱，不交钱不许看。

Incense smoke hangs at the mouth of a limestone cave in the forest. Inside stands a stalagmite shaped like a stooping man. A wandering Taoist who keeps the cave says it is one of the Qianli guards: he rested here ten years ago, the Gu King turned him to stone, and the dripping limestone wrapped him up drop by drop. Villagers come to burn incense and pray to the 'Stone Guard' to bring their travellers home. The Taoist's hired toughs guard the offering box. No coin, no look.
after: 打手被打跑，道士还想狡辩，一个老石匠一句话就把他问住了：钟乳石一年才长零点几毫米，十年也就一两毫米，要把一个人裹起来，少说要几千年。「这根石人，比寨子还老。」功德箱里翻出一块半砖，是道士从蛊骑那里买来当「法器」的。

The toughs chased off, the Taoist tries to argue, and an old stonemason who came along silences him with one question. Dripstone grows a fraction of a millimetre a year; in ten years it adds a millimetre or two at most, and to wrap up a whole man would take thousands of years at the very least. 'That stone man is older than the village.' In the offering box you find a half brick the Taoist bought from the riders as a 'holy relic'.

name: 围会营
The Siege Camp
before: 寨老会四周扎着一圈营帐，蛊王的人把会堂围得水泄不通：寨丁守路，吹箭手爬在树上，蛊骑在外圈来回巡。会堂里偶尔传出几声咳嗽，是寨老们在里头熬着。营里架着几口大锅炖肉，香气被故意往会堂那边扇。

A ring of tents encircles the Elders' Council house, and the Gu King's men have it sealed tight: guards on the paths, blowgunners up the trees, riders circling outside. Now and then a cough drifts from the house, the elders holding out within. The camp has great pots of meat stewing, and someone is fanning the smell toward the council house on purpose.
after: 围营被你们冲开，锅里的肉都给寨老会送了进去。会堂的门开了一条缝，阿梅的黄狗第一个钻了出来。七个寨老扶着门框站着，一个比一个瘦，最老的那个被扶在中间，怀里抱着一只木匣，抱得紧紧的。

You break the siege, and the stewed meat goes in to the council. The door opens a crack and A Mei's yellow dog is first out. Seven elders stand holding the door frame, each thinner than the last, the oldest supported in the middle, a wooden box clasped tight against his chest.

name: 寨老会
The Elders' Council
before: 寨老会是一座九根柱子的大吊脚楼，七寨的大事都在这里商量。围营虽破，蛊王的一队精兵还守在楼下，堵着楼梯，扬言谁上楼就烧楼。楼上，九十三岁的岩公坐在火塘边，身后是三百格的竹架，码满了半块茶砖，每块拴着一根竹签。七寨的粮换金买卖从前就在这楼下过秤，如今楼下只剩刀枪。

The Elders' Council is a great stilt house on nine pillars where the seven villages settle their weighty matters. The siege is broken, but a squad of the Gu King's elite still holds the stairs and swears to burn the house if anyone climbs them. Upstairs, ninety-three-year-old Yan Gong sits by the hearth with a rack of three hundred pigeonholes behind him, stacked with half bricks, a bamboo tag on each. The seven villages used to weigh their grain-for-gold trade under this house. Now there's nothing under it but blades.
after:
精兵被打退，楼下的秤又挂了起来。寨里有粮，河里淘得出金沙，粮换金的买卖重新开张。

岩公让你们把车上那半块茶砖拿上来。他在竹架上一格一格地摸过去，摸到最后一格，抽出一块，跟你们那块一合，严丝合缝。二百九十九根签都写着名字，只有这一块的签是空的。「宋副镖头说，这一块，等后头的人拿着另一半来合。」岩公数了数架子，又叹口气：「还空着十几格，是这些年被偷走的。」

The elite driven off, the scales hang under the house again. The villages have grain and the river yields gold dust, so trade in grain for gold reopens.  Yan Gong asks you to bring up the half brick from your cart. He feels his way along the rack pigeonhole by pigeonhole, reaches the last, draws out a half, and fits it to yours. It closes without a crack. Two hundred and ninety-nine tags carry names; this one's tag alone is blank. 'Deputy Song said this one waits for whoever comes after with the other half.' Yan Gong counts along the rack and sighs. 'A dozen and more still empty. Stolen, over the years.'
